prompt: Under which conditions does a hail claim qualify for the Fast Lane, and what must the Fast Lane confirmation say about the deductible?
expected_response: CG-FL-1 (Fast Lane criteria): a claim enters the Fast Lane when all of the following hold -- glass or dents only, estimate below EUR 1,000, policy ACTIVE on the event date, hail cover HC-7 set; it is auto-confirmed without an adjuster and the Fast Lane never pays out. PW-DED-1 (Deductible rules): the confirmation must state the deductible amount (usually EUR 150, 300 or 500), which is charged once per event and is never waived by an automated decision.

prompt: How often is the deductible charged under hail cover clause HC-7, and what happens under the repair network clause RN-3 when no partner slot is offered within five working days after the FNOL?
expected_response: PW-HC-7 (Hail cover HC-7): the deductible from the policy schedule applies once per hail event, regardless of the number of damaged panels or repair steps; glass repaired through the partner network is settled without deductible. PW-RN-3 (Repair network steering clause): in return for a 15 percent premium discount Acme proposes a partner and a repair slot after the FNOL; if no partner slot is offered within 5 working days after FNOL, the customer's free choice of workshop applies and the discount stays. A waiting list entry does not count as a slot proposal.

prompt: What is the hail total-loss signature under clause TL-1, and where must a claim in the Total Loss Fastlane not be queued?
expected_response: PW-TL-1 (Total loss definition): a vehicle is a total loss when the repair estimate exceeds 70 percent of the replacement value on the day of loss, or when the intake evidence shows glass shattered and roof deformed with more than 150 dents; either criterion is sufficient on its own. CG-TL-2 (Total Loss Fastlane): the customer is contacted within one working day, the assistance partner picks up the vehicle, a remote valuation follows and the settlement target is 5 working days; a Fastlane claim is not assigned to a drive-in center or a body shop and must not sit in an AWAITING_WORKSHOP_SLOT queue.

prompt: Which fraud indicators does the claims guideline list for hail claims, when is the drive-in scanner mismatch flag set, and who decides on a claim that shows indicators?
expected_response: CG-FR-5 (Fraud indicators guideline) lists: photo EXIF timestamps before the event date of the cell, the same VIN reported through two channels within 48 hours, a workshop estimate more than 25 percent above the contracted rate, identical line-item texts across claims of one workshop, and a scanner count deviating by more than 50 percent from the dents claimed. CG-SC-1 (Drive-in scanner results handling): the mismatch flag is set when the scanned count deviates by more than 50 percent from the count claimed at intake, and a mismatch is not a refusal. Per CG-FR-5 every indicator is a reason to look, not a verdict: a single indicator proves nothing, the overall picture decides, a human specialist decides; claims with indicators go ON_HOLD to the fraud specialist while all other claims are released on the normal track.

prompt: What does the BaFin processing-time rule require, what happens on day 20, and why is drive-in partner P-DELLENDOC inactive -- can it still be activated for a hail event?
expected_response: CG-BAFIN-30 (Processing-time rule): BaFin expects a decision on every claim within 30 days after the first notice of loss and volume is no excuse; on day 20 every claim without a decision is escalated to the claims lead of the line, on day 25 open claims are reported to the head of claims, and claims held for a fraud specialist are not exempt. PC-DELLENDOC-2024 (Drive-in contract P-DELLENDOC): the partner (90 scans per day, tier STANDARD) is INACTIVE since 2026-01-01 because the parts-channel clause PC-4 is unsigned; while inactive it receives no assignments, but the interim contract template IC-2 allows a 48 hour activation under the old 2024 terms for NatCat events, for at most 60 days.
